utterances.text: And you were also appointed a member of the command, and which office did you hold there in the command of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: I was appointed to the same office as in the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade with somewhat broader jurisdiction, if I may put it that way, that is, those were affairs which had to do with logistics and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to show a document to the witness. It is one of the documents which the Prosecution tendered as a Zagreb document. All I want is -- this is one of the rare lists with the nominees for the brigade command, and I would merely like to ask the witness to tell us if that is it. This document was not admitted. You refused to admit the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want it admitted now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think so, yes. Because this is one of the rare documents confirming the date of the brigade formation, even though there are some other documents. I want to show this witness because of some names of some persons, to see what he knows about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Give it to the witness. We'll consider the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the last sentence below -- after the table and above the signature. And when you look at the names and the composition, what can you tell us about this? Was this, indeed, the state of affairs on that date, 15th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what is the difference?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I notice here that this is a proposal, that these are merely nominations for members of the command of the Vitez Brigade intended for the Croat Defence Council or, rather, the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So am I right when I say that this is not the final composition?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right. This is not the final composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is merely a proposal, a plan?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a plan. A plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For instance, did you happen to see which persons from this list of the future composition were not appointed to those posts, for instance?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for instance, 8, Stipo Zigonjic, he was never a member of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: And number 14, Franjo Alilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Incidentally, under number 8, that is assistant chief of organisation of personnel who assumed the responsibility for those affairs?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: For those affairs, it was Mrs. Gordana --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You mean Gordana Badrov, do you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Gordana Badrov.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when did she join?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, some five or six days later, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. I would, nevertheless, like to adduce this document and seek its admission, except that there is a confusion in the translation where it says "formational duty," "formation duty," it says "commander" and then it says "brigade colonel" and in English, it says, "brigadier," but that is not correct. It should be colonel, brigade colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. No objection from us if Mr. Cerkez wants that in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We proposed this document originally, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would have saved a great deal of time had you said that you were going to put this document in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour; when witnesses were coming, I was searching the database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Would it keep the same number, Z number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, the Z number, Z544.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, I think we could now move on to the critical events themselves, that is to say, the 15th or, rather, the 16th of April, 1993. Can you tell us in two or three words about the very eve of the conflict between the HVO and the BH army in Vitez? In what situation was the brigade when the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the brigade was incomplete. The command was incomplete. Incomplete, just being set up. It was not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that moment, just before the conflict broke out, what is the maximum number of men that the brigade could count on? How many were on the lists of persons who were mobilised until then for going for shifts at the front line to fight against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said just now. In addition to the incomplete command, we had one battalion. Actually, this was the 2nd Battalion of the former -- I mean, the second former battalion of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. It had about 260 to 300 men at a maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness Zuljevic, please, until the conflict broke out, were these men, this estimated number of men that you gave us just now, were they ever all mobilised at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Zuljevic, you, personally, as a citizen of Vitez and having had the information you did have as a member of the brigade, did you expect that there could be a frontal conflict between the two sides in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Me, personally? My friends and my colleagues from the command and I, we never could have imagined anything like that. We never could have believed that there would be a conflict, let alone one of such proportions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In connection with that, Mr. Zuljevic, when you say, "My friends and I," did this include only local persons or were there also people who came as refugees and other people from other municipalities who had to come because of the war and who were forced to come?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They also felt that way. You probably know how things developed. There were some people there from Kotor Varos who had been expelled by the Serbs, by the former Yugoslav Peoples' Army, who partly stayed in the territory of the municipality of Vitez, and not only them. Generally speaking, the population is mixed where we live.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. In the months prior to the conflict, we heard quite a bit of evidence here concerning various incidents. To the best of your knowledge, and in your assessment, which one of the two ethnic groups was the perpetrator of these incidents, who caused these incidents to happen, or was it both sides? What was this all about?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as incidents are concerned, it was hard to tell because both one side and the other were equally to blame for such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were the victims in these incidents from both ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were the perpetrators of these things also from both ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that, as far as perpetrators are concerned, from the Croat side, that they were directed by someone to bring about these incidents?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What was the reason, then? Why did such individuals appear and commit these things? How did you explain this to yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you just now. There were other people there too, refugees. Everybody thought they were right. This was resolving certain relationships on an individual basis. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, this does not appear, this point does not appear in the summary, and I don't see how it has anything to do with the rejoinder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's just get on with it. Yes, come on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are going further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, on the 15th of April, in the evening, 1993, where were you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: I was assistant duty officer at the command of the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were you on duty by yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who was on duty with you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Sucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What happened in the evening? As compared to the previous tours of duty, was there anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: In the early evening hours, we had a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who took part in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, first we received information from the Operative Zone that we should bring the entire command together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you manage to bring the entire command together?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How many people managed to get there?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: About five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did Cerkez come to that meeting too once you were all there?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you exactly, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez conveyed to us then that upon the order -- or rather, he got information from the commander of the Operative Zone that there were indications that we should bring everybody from the command together and that a possible attack is being expected - of course, according to the information received - from the directions of Kruscica and Vranjska, with the objective of attacking parts of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that time, did Mario Cerkez say what the task of the brigade was in terms of that particular estimate?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What task was this?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Our task, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: The task of our brigade was, in terms of all of us who were there, was to prevent a possible attack from Kruscica and Vranjska, an attack on town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And who was supposed to carry out this order?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: This order was supposed to be carried out by the commander of the 1st Battalion, Anto Bertovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness. Could you please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in any other way in the realisation of this order; you, personally?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. I was the duty officer and we worked together on the realisation of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Necessary information, contacts, telephone calls, was all of this done from the headquarters of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were you in contact with the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When the meeting was over, did your colleagues discuss this, I mean this alarm, this raising of the level of -- the degree of readiness? Did you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did. We did not -- I mean, how should I put this? We did not take this as some kind of danger, because, before, there were similar reports that proved to be untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, how long did Cerkez stay at headquarters then, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe - I don't know - perhaps an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Later on, during the course of the evening or night, did he return to headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps once, but I did not register that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Before this meeting that you spoke about, did you have an opportunity of seeing Cerkez during the course of the day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you hear anything about Cerkez being at a meeting between the representatives of the politicians, or rather, the civilian authorities of both sides, the HVO and the BiH army, and the military representatives of both sides?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately when this happened during the course of that day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime in the afternoon, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you have some information about how many people, approximately, participated in this meeting, and where it took place?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. No, I have no information in relation to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information about the successful outcome of that meeting, at least, in general?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, people talked, but -- I'm not sure. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So what you found out indirectly, as people talked, as you said, was this promising or did this cause concern?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was promising, but I don't know about any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember perhaps that this was mentioned on local radio that evening?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. At headquarters, we had a TV set. We did not listen to the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened in the morning, please?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: The 16th of April, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: In the early morning hours, loud detonations were heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Shells were falling all over town, and even in the very centre of town and near the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could gunfire be heard as well?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Gunfire was heard too, coming from all sides, primarily the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reliable information as to what was going on in the field?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: We did not have any reliable information as to what was going on in the field, but since the intensity was high, it was clear to us that the BH army had undertaken significant activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When did Cerkez come to headquarters in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Cerkez came in the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: During the course of the morning, did you have a meeting again? Did your commander convene you for another meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When was this, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was sometime in the morning, around 9.00 or 10.00. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What was the point of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: The point of that meeting was primarily the following: In line with orders, oral orders issued by Blaskic, we make a maximum effort to collect as much information as possible from the territory of our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what did you do then? What kind of activities did you embark upon in order to carry out this assignment?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: We tried, first of all, through the command of our battalion. Then Mr. Mario explicitly requested us to contact the other units too that were in the territory of the municipality of Vitez. And all other information, regardless of where they may come from, from civilians, locals, coordinators in villages, coordinators of village guards, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can we say, in terms of what you said just now, that you started collecting information by drawing on all available sources; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were you asked to compile reports in writing about this?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. That was within the order to collect all information and to convey this every two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me try to make sense of this. Who was the commander who convened the meeting at 9.00 or 10.00?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And what, simply, put simply, were the orders which he gave?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mario Cerkez issued orders orally. There weren't any orders in writing. Since there was chaos all over, we were all there together in one room, and we were then told that we should draw on our own acquaintances, friends, this and that person, that we should get in contact with all persons on duty. We tried with the Vitezovi and the military police to gather as much information as possible in order to compile a report with regard to this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We need this for the transcript; could you please repeat this, and to send it where? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: To the commander of the Operative Zone of that military district.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that is Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to give the witness three documents; Z673.7, then after that, Z673.6, and Z694.4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness is being asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You have been asked to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Kovacic now speak into the microphone. The interpreters cannot hear him either now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: These three documents that I have requested are three reports of the brigade from the 16th of April at 10.00, at 12.00, and the last one on the 17th of April at 4.30. These are the Zagreb documents. They were not handed over to the Office of the Prosecutor. Mr. Zuljevic, please cast a glance at this document. First of all, tell me, do you specifically remember this report perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I can't remember this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My next question: When you look at the heading, the signature, the date, the number, the way in which it was written, does this look like a report of the Viteska Brigade? Could it be one or could it not be one?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It could be a report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to draw your attention to the second paragraph of this text. You use a formulation to the effect of "our forces"?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "our forces"?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we all gathered information from the field and I repeat once again, there was chaos at headquarters as well. However, when we say "our," what is meant is forces of the HVO, forces of the members of the Croat people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. This formulation is repeated again in the second sentence, so let me ask you: Did any unit of the Viteska Brigade, was any force of the Viteska Brigade involved in action in Donja Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was any group or unit of yours in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In Sivrino Selo?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. Not in Sivrino Selo, not in Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, again, it says "our forces," and there are three persons who are killed that are mentioned. Do you remember, Mr. Zuljevic, that morning by 10.00, was there a single soldier from the brigade, a single member of the brigade who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. Not a single soldier on that first day, as far as I can remember, got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How do you then interpret this "our forces"? "We have sustained losses," or, rather, "We have had three persons who were killed," et cetera. Whose people are these?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I specifically do not remember whose they could be, I mean who got this information, but it could pertain to someone else who was operating in the territory of the municipality of Vitez. At any rate, it's not from the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In this way, do you include the entire Croat side?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So regardless of which unit is being referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You personally, Mr. Zuljevic -- you can put the document away, never mind. Did you take part, actively, in this elaboration of such information?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since I happened to be at headquarters that morning, I was a witness of this gathering of information. However, we were on the telephone for the most part, whereas the operations people conducted this and collected information for reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You, who were involved in these telephone contacts, how did you convey information to your colleagues who were writing the reports?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was lots of commotion, confusion. We had this notebook where we wrote all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What did you write?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, all the information we got, all movements, changes, everything that happened, of course, to the extent to which we could find out about this in the territory of our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher now to show this document to the witness, please. The previous document was 673.7. This one is 673.6.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will Mr. Kovacic speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you speak into the microphone, Mr. Kovacic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, will you now have a look at this document. Look at when was this issued, the heading, all the other elements.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this before? Would you identify the document?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, like the previous one, except that I see that in the heading of this document there is absent -- we don't see that it was issued by the Vitez Brigade. It says "Croatian Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that is why it doesn't look quite regular to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Will you again now look again. We have the third paragraph. And I think we have here the report that "Our three soldiers were killed," and this report was written only two hours after the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it is those, the same three soldiers, and perhaps these are new three soldiers. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember that you received any reports from Poculica that morning, where Croats were under -- from which Croats were expelled under the pressure of the BH army? It is under item 3. Do you know anything about those events?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do. We did not have a report from Poculica. We had information from people who had arrived from Poculica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I don't think we have to go into that. Could the witness now be shown the third document, Z694.4. It was also adduced together with other Zagreb documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, this was issued the next day. Have a look and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, it's 4.00. Thank God you said at the beginning that you were going to be brief, because if you had not said that, I don't know where we would be. I suppose you're going to complete the examination-in-chief now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise, Your Honour. I simply made the wrong forecast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because I believe that the witness will have to come back, but at least please complete the examination-in-chief, because we've gone right beyond the time estimates you gave us in the written document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need only two minutes with this document and then I will be over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, same question as before. This document was issued the next day, around half past two. Have you seen this document before, and can you either say yes or no, is this a document issued by the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will Mr. Kovacic speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, you're being asked to speak into a microphone yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Now it is switched off. We are sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now it's working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was my fault. But if everybody speaks into the microphone, we're going to get on more quickly. Yes. Can you try to finish in ten minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zuljevic, to save time, as with the previous reports. Now, on the second day, did the technology change, from what you can see, or do you still report on all the developments in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Here, in the beginning, I again see that in the heading "Vitez Brigade" is missing, and I see the signature and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you say if this is a document of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can, perhaps I can't. There is the signature, but this copy is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us assume that this is an authentic document. But my main question: In view of the wording, would you say that the same method is applied again, that all the developments in Vitez are described, regardless of whether your units are at a particular site or somebody else, that is, civilians, Croats, other units, or whoever?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And not to go further into that report, because the Chamber has seen some later reports of the brigade, but I have just one more question about this. Mr. Zuljevic, in subsequent brigade reports which were available to you when you were on duty from time to time, in those later reports, is it specified -- were such reports written who it is about, that is, which troops are involved somewhere in one operation or other, or do you -- is it the term "our forces" again?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. It was specified precisely who it is, what unit he or they belonged to, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How many days did you spend in the -- on the premises of the brigade command, intensively?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, those two or three days, the first -- the initial ones, until we organised ourselves better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And after that, where did you spend your time?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Since I was with the logistics sector, I spent my time on the premises of the logistics sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now my last question, or rather two or three questions related to this. Since that was your field of operation, and you should know these things, what kind of vehicles did you have available on the eve of the conflict and in the early days of the conflict? What kind of vehicles did you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, come. The command of the brigade and the brigade as such had only one small car for the officers, for their tours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what make was it? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: It was a Lada Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It is a passenger vehicle, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a passenger vehicle, a field vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps have a dark blue Audi?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did the brigade, or rather did the brigade have or use any passenger vans?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The 4th Military Police Battalion, was, if I may put it that way, was your neighbour to the logistics; it was right next to the logistics sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How far from you was it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was next to our building, about 20 metres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And did the military police have vans to transport its personnel?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They did have a couple of -- three or four vans, but a couple of vans were there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, in those early days of the war, do you ever remember that the military police asked you to lend them a van, that is, to get it from somewhere and then put it at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP ZULJEVIC
utterances.text: No. They solved those things by themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions about Mr. Mario Cerkez. I believe that other witnesses have already said enough, and there is no need to ask this witness about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That may be a convenient moment. We'll adjourn now till tomorrow morning for cross-examination. After that, we'll deal with the various outstanding administrative matters. Mr. Lopez-Terres, confine, if you will, your cross-examination to no more than the examination-in-chief, which was an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be shorter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zuljevic, would you be back, please, to complete your evidence, tomorrow at half past 9.00 in the morning. Would you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include members of the Defence team. We'll adjourn now till tomorrow morning.
